text:
I took my girlfriend with COVID-19 to get tested and get a medical certificate.
When I arrived, a staff member greeted me with a pleasant smile. She was a slightly chubby woman wearing a blue dress. She had me wait for about 15 minutes, then finally called me to take her blood pressure and other measurements. She was having my girlfriend take her temperature, and she was telling me to wait. Then she disappeared. After a while, a woman in a black shirt with slightly wavy hair walked in with an unwilling expression. I wasn't sure if she was a doctor. If she was, she probably should have bought a license to practice instead of relying on her knowledge. Her words, tone, and facial expression were something like, "If you can't test me, I can't give you a certificate." My girlfriend asked if she could get tested, and she said, "There's no place to test, I can't test, I can't give you a certificate." Even though I was already prepared for the harsh language of doctors and nurses in the community, I didn't expect her tone and facial expression to be this bad. She didn't even look like she was disgusted. Oh, and the worst part was that I had already stated my purpose from the beginning. If they couldn't do it, I should have told them from the beginning. Now, she's making me wait, taking measurements, and taking my medical history, wasting my time for hours, and then she can't tell me. It's so awful. And the last thing she said was, "Go get tested at San Kamphaeng Hospital." But it's a bit expensive. Sorry, but you can afford it.
(Morning of January 24, 2024)
